items.stem: What is the core shift when moving from individual contributor to manager?

options.text: Results now come largely through other people rather than your own output
options.rationale: Correct: a manager's impact is achieved through the team, not solo delivery.

options.text: You stop being accountable for any results
options.rationale: Managers remain accountable for team outcomes.
Technical judgment still helps, even if it is no longer the main job.

options.text: You should personally do all the hardest tasks yourself
options.rationale: Hoarding the hard work is a classic new-manager trap.

items.explanation: Correct: a manager's impact is achieved through the team, not solo delivery.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: You delegate a task but find yourself making every decision on it. This most likely means you:

options.text: Delegated the task without delegating enough authority
options.rationale: Correct: effective delegation passes appropriate decision authority, not just the work.

options.text: Chose the wrong person and should take it back
options.rationale: The issue is the authority given, not necessarily the person.
The fix is clearer delegation, not avoiding it.

options.text: Need to add more approval steps
options.rationale: More approvals increase, not reduce, the micromanagement.

items.explanation: Correct: effective delegation passes appropriate decision authority, not just the work.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make feedback more effective? (Select TWO)

options.text: Giving it promptly and tied to specific behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: timely, specific feedback is easier to act on.

options.text: Focusing on the behaviour and its impact rather than the person's character
options.rationale: Correct: behaviour-and-impact feedback is constructive and less defensive.

options.text: Storing all feedback for a single annual review
options.rationale: Delayed, batched feedback loses relevance and impact.

options.text: Keeping it vague so the person is not discouraged
options.rationale: Vague feedback gives nothing concrete to change.

items.explanation: Correct: timely, specific feedback is easier to act on.; Correct: behaviour-and-impact feedback is constructive and less defensive.
